fixes.explanation: Yes. John says, "For He knew who would betray Him." That is why Jesus said, "Not all of you are clean." Jesus isn't guessing here, because He knows. And He washed those feet anyway.
John doesn't mention anyone running late, friend. He says, "For He knew who would betray Him." That is why Jesus said, "Not all of you are clean." The reason is the betrayal.

The Passover Feast tells us when this happens. It's just before the Feast, but it isn't where His love stops. John says Jesus "…loved them to the very end." The Feast tells us when, and the end tells us how far.

Yes, baker. John says "…the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus." That's heavy, so I'll say it plainly and leave it there. Notice the word "already." The meal was underway, and this was already in Judas' heart.
Pontius Pilate was the governor (Matthew 27:2), so he's a real name in Jesus' story. But John 13:2 doesn't name him here. The text says it was the devil who put this into Judas' heart.
There was a King Herod when Jesus was born (Matthew 2:1), so that's a real name in Jesus' story. But John doesn't name him in this verse. John says the devil put it into Judas' heart to betray Jesus.
A cup would be a very long evening for all those feet. John says Jesus "…poured water into a basin…" That's the vessel in this verse.

That's it. Jesus tells Peter, "You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand." So Peter doesn't realize it yet, and Jesus promises that understanding is coming. Plenty of my batches made sense only after they came out of the oven.
Yep. Peter tells Him, "Never shall You wash my feet!" Jesus just said understanding would come later, and Peter answers with a flat no. I think that's a bold thing to say to the Lord.
Jesus is the one who mentions later: "…later you will understand." Peter doesn't say he'll wait. He answers, "Never shall You wash my feet!" That's a refusal of the washing itself.
Right. Peter says, "Then, Lord, not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!" He heard "…you have no part with Me." and answered right away. He asks for more than just his feet.
It's true, friend. Jesus says, "You call Me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so, because I am." He agrees with the titles. And He had already washed their feet when He said it.
Right. Jesus quotes the Scripture: "The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me." (Psalm 41:9) So it's someone who shares His bread. That's close, and it's why this hurts to read.
There's no soldier in the quote, friend. Jesus says, "The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me." (Psalm 41:9) The person described is one who shares His bread.
